Streets, schools and getting around Edmonds

items.t: Edmonds is in southeast Burnaby, centred on Kingsway at Edmonds Street around Edmonds Station, and is one of Burnaby's four town centres. "Edmonds" is the GVR board sub-area name (listings also label it "Edmonds BE"). The City publishes no street-by-street MLS boundary; the Edmonds Community Plan (adopted March 2025) plans the centre in six districts — Central Edmonds, South Edmonds, the Station District, West Edmonds, Northwest Edmonds and East Edmonds.

Main roads: Kingsway and Edmonds Street, with Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue serving the station area and Canada Way / 10th Avenue linking east toward New Westminster. Royal Oak and Metrotown are to the west, Highgate sits within the town centre's east side, and South Slope is to the south-west.

Where the condo stock concentrates: (1) the Kingsway / Highgate node — the Kings Crossing towers by Cressey at Kingsway and Edmonds Street, and the older low-rise stock on Edmonds Street itself (Toscana); (2) South Edmonds / Southgate City — Ledingham McAllister's master-planned node south of the station (Azure, Azure 2, and the Cedar Creek low-rise community on 14th Avenue / 15th Street / 16th Street). Interior streets away from Kingsway remain detached houses.

At the Burnaby community level that month, condos & townhomes posted a median sale price of $686,000, $763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list and 36 days on market (SnapStats GVR September 2026 — community-level figures only; no sub-area median is published).

Transit anchor: Edmonds Station on the Expo Line, with a bus loop; TransLink route 116 also links Edmonds Station to Metrotown Station via Imperial, Sussex, Marine Drive, Marine Way, Byrne Road, Southridge Drive, Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue, serving south Edmonds street by street.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Edmonds

items.t: Burnaby zoning and plans: the governing bylaw is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, adopted June 9, 2026 and in effect July 1, 2026 — the former Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 (1965) is not current and must not be cited as current. Burnaby's R1 SSMUH District (June 2024) allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, with multi-unit lots able to be stratified. The Edmonds Community Plan was adopted in March 2025, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025) replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict.

blocks.text: Good to know about Edmonds

items.t: Azure carries three addresses. The strata address in listings is 7683 Park Crescent, the developer's presentation centre was at 7662 18th Street, and unit listings also appear at 7788 18th Street — one building, three addresses in the wild. Confirm which address the specific unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents.
Southgate City is a 15-to-20-year build-out, and Azure is only phase one.

Cedar Creek's buildings were phased a year apart. Listings date 7133 14th Avenue to 2021, 7579 16th Street to 2022 and 7599 15th Street to 2023 — same developer, same community name, three different warranty and depreciation-report positions. Compare the specific building's documents, not the community's marketing.

The town centre got a brand-new plan in 2025 — and then the citywide OCP changed over it. The Edmonds Community Plan was adopted in March 2025; the Burnaby 2050 OCP followed on December 9, 2025 and takes precedence over older community-plan maps where they conflict; the Kingsway + Edmonds master plan is expressly under review to align with the new OCP. Listing copy citing pre-2025 Edmonds planning is out of date.

Route 116 is the south Edmonds workhorse. Beyond the SkyTrain, TransLink route 116 runs Metrotown Station to Edmonds Station via Griffiths Drive, Southridge Drive and 18th Avenue — the bus the Cedar Creek and Southgate streets actually live on, and the one listing copy rarely names.
Burnaby is also rebuilding the cycling network through the town centre.

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: (1) the Stride Avenue corridor south of the station — Riverstone, Kensington, Eden at Edmonds, Maplewood Terrace, Sylvan Court on Edmonds Street itself; (2) the 17th Avenue / Leeside node — Leeside Creek, Element 1 and Element 2; (3) the South Edmonds / 14th–16th Avenue edge of Southgate City — Kingsgate Gardens and the Southgate townhomes at 7333 16th Avenue. blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Edmonds

items.t: Form B diligence (all 11 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern. The age split is the diligence point here: Kensington (1992) and Sylvan Court (1990) are deep into depreciation-report cycles while Element 2 (2025) is in first-cycle and warranty years.

blocks.text: Good to know about Edmonds

items.t: Two complexes share the street number 7128 — on different streets. Leeside Creek is at 7128 17th Avenue (2005) and Riverstone is at 7128 Stride Avenue (2003). Document orders, courier directions and even listing searches routinely cross them; confirm the street, not just the number, before ordering a Form B.

Southgate City is a 15-to-20-year build-out, and the townhouses predate the towers. The 7333 16th Avenue townhouse complex (2007) and Kingsgate Gardens (2010) were built years before Azure, Southgate City's first tower phase, completed in 2024 — a Southgate townhouse buyer owns the low-rise edge of a master plan whose later towers still require separate rezonings.

Edmonds Community Centre is the amenity the strata fees don't buy. At 7433 Edmonds Street it has a 6-lane pool, a leisure pool with waterslides and a lazy river, steam room and sauna, two gyms and the Edmonds Centre for 55+; the Tommy Douglas Library branch serves this quadrant at the Kingsway node and the Edmonds UPCC is at #201-7315 Edmonds St — the civic package beside the Stride/17th Avenue complexes.

The ravine is the south edge's diligence item. Byrne Creek Ravine Park runs south from the town centre along Byrne Creek, and Ron McLean Park sits at the area's south side by the ravine — for lots and complexes backing onto the ravine, watercourse setbacks and development-permit conditions surface late in deals if not checked early.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Edmonds
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Lot character: typical lot sizes are UNVERIFIED at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only lot-size figures a source states are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: 280 m² and 281 m². The lot character that is documented is positional, not dimensional: Kingsway/station-node lots are planned under the March 2025 Edmonds Community Plan's six districts, and ravine-edge lots carry Byrne Creek setback diligence.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Edmonds is confirmed in the research; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission, UNVERIFIED for individual lots. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Market context, labelled correctly: Burnaby IS a SnapStats-covered community — Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined only. SnapStats has NO land category, and no detached figure is a land figure. September 2026 context only: Edmonds sub-area detached inventory 9 / solds 2 (22% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" 89 / 7 (8%); Burnaby community detached median $1,825,000 and attached median $686,000. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only).

items.t: Edmonds is a City of Burnaby sub-area in southeast Burnaby, centred on Kingsway at Edmonds Street around Edmonds Station, and is one of Burnaby's four town centres. "Edmonds" is the GVR board sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the Edmonds Community Plan (adopted March 2025) plans the town centre in districts including Central Edmonds, South Edmonds, the Station District, West Edmonds, Northwest Edmonds and East Edmonds, with Northwest Edmonds generally bounded by Gilley Avenue to the west, Walker Avenue / Griffiths Avenue to the east, Imperial Street to the north and Beresford Street to the south.
Nearby areas: Royal Oak and Metrotown to the west, Highgate within the town centre's east side, East Burnaby and the City of New Westminster to the east, South Slope to the south-west.

Main roads and transit: Kingsway and Edmonds Street are the main roads, with Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue serving the station area and Canada Way / 10th Avenue linking east toward New Westminster. Edmonds Station is on the Expo Line; route 116 runs between Metrotown Station and Edmonds Station via Griffiths Drive, Southridge Drive and 18th Avenue. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors: Edmonds Community Centre, 7433 Edmonds Street (pools, gyms, Edmonds Centre for 55+); the Tommy Douglas Library at the Kingsway town-centre node; the Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre at #201-7315 Edmonds St; Byrne Creek Ravine Park and Taylor Park, 7599 Mission Ave, at the east side. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, north-west across the city.

items.t: OCP and community plan — Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025: replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict; the Edmonds Community Plan was adopted in March 2025 and plans the centre in six districts (Central Edmonds, South Edmonds, the Station District, West Edmonds, Northwest Edmonds, East Edmonds). A town-centre lot's value case is read off these two documents, in that order.

Watercourse diligence: Byrne Creek runs in a ravine through the area's south side (Byrne Creek Ravine Park; Ron McLean Park, 7820 Hedley Ave, at the south side). A floodplain designation for Edmonds' residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read; parcel-level hazard, watercourse-setback and ALR status are property-specific checks — for lots backing onto the ravine, check watercourse setbacks and development-permit conditions early, because setback surprises surface late in deals.

blocks.text: Good to know about Edmonds

items.t: The town centre got two new governing documents in nine months: the Edmonds Community Plan in March 2025 and the Burnaby 2050 OCP on December 9, 2025 — and the Kingsway + Edmonds master plan is explicitly under review to align with the new OCP, so a land memo written off the pre-2025 plan framework is stale on its face.

Southgate's townhouses predate its towers by 17 years: the 7333 16th Avenue townhouse complex (2007) and Kingsgate Gardens (2010) were built years before Azure, Southgate City's first tower phase, completed in 2024 — a Southgate-edge lot or townhouse sits at the low-rise edge of a master plan whose later towers still require separate rezonings.

The bus the South Edmonds streets actually live on is route 116: Metrotown Station to Edmonds Station via Imperial, Sussex, Marine Drive, Marine Way, Byrne Road, Southridge Drive, Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue — the street-by-street service behind the station-area lots, and the route listing copy rarely names.

faq.a: Yes. Edmonds is one of Burnaby's four town centres, centred on Kingsway at Edmonds Street around Edmonds Station on the Expo Line, and the City adopted a new Edmonds Community Plan in March 2025.

faq.q: Which schools serve an Edmonds address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. In-area SD41 schools include Edmonds Community Elementary (K–7), 7651 18th Ave, Twelfth Avenue Elementary (K–7) and Byrne Creek Community Secondary (8–12), 7777 18th St; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.
Edmonds Station is on the Expo Line with a bus loop; route 116 also links Edmonds Station to Metrotown Station through south Burnaby via Griffiths Drive, Southridge Drive and Marine Way.

faq.q: What is happening at Kingsway and Edmonds?
faq.a: The City and BC Housing are planning the publicly owned 4.5-acre southwest corner: replacing Hall Towers' 331 units without displacing tenants, plus over 1,400 purpose-built rental units and approximately 1,000 market strata units; the plan is under review to align with the Burnaby 2050 OCP.

faq.q: Kingsway towers or Southgate — what's the real difference?
faq.a: Vintage and form. The Kingsway node is Cressey's Kings Crossing towers (Tower 2 built 2020) plus the 2012 wood-frame Toscana low-rise; South Edmonds is Ledingham McAllister's Southgate City (Azure and Azure 2, completed 2024) and its Cedar Creek low-rises (2021–2023). All of it prices off the same Burnaby attached median ($686,000, September 2026), but warranty status, construction (concrete vs wood-frame) and depreciation-report cycles differ building by building.

faq.q: Toscana says "No Pets or Rentals" — can I rent it out? Can I bring a dog?
faq.a: Renting, yes for a long-term tenancy: rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. The pet prohibition is different — pet bylaws remain enforceable, and a current Toscana listing records pets as "No." Treat the rental line as void and the pet line as live until the registered bylaws on the Form B say otherwise.

faq.q: Are pets allowed in the newer buildings?
faq.a: Full pet bylaws (numbers, size, dogs) are UNCONFIRMED from public sources for all three — read the registered bylaws.

faq.q: How far is the SkyTrain, honestly?
faq.a: Edmonds Station is on the Expo Line.

faq.q: Is Hall Towers a condo building I can buy into?
faq.a: No. Hall Towers (7264 Kingsway) is 331 units of BC Housing non-market rental housing owned by the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation — there is nothing to buy, and it is slated for replacement under the Kingsway + Edmonds master plan without displacing tenants.

faq.q: Stride Avenue or 17th Avenue — where is the townhouse choice?
faq.a: Both corridors: Stride Avenue carries Riverstone (2003), Kensington (1992), Eden at Edmonds (2012) and Maplewood Terrace (2006), with Sylvan Court (1990) on Edmonds Street; 17th Avenue carries Leeside Creek (2005), Element 1 (2020) and Element 2 (2025). The Stride stock is older and larger-complex; the 17th Avenue stock is the station-side newer product.

faq.q: Can I rent out my Edmonds townhouse?
faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Kensington's listing data already records rentals allowed. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.

faq.q: How far is the SkyTrain, honestly?
faq.a: Element 2's marketing puts Edmonds Station 600 m away; Leeside Creek listings put the walk at 5 minutes; Kensington is described as a short stroll to Edmonds SkyTrain Station. Edmonds Station is on the Expo Line. Measure the walk for the specific complex — the Stride Avenue addresses sit farther south than the 17th Avenue ones.
